Round 5 passes all seven checks (R5-1 to R5-7), and I tested it in the real app. Separately, I found two low-severity bugs that are outside this round's scope and don't change the PASS.

| Check | Result | What I saw |
|---|---|---|
| R5-1 red/green | PASS | With the old `FileList.tsx`, 4 of 6 render tests fail: (a), (b) and (c) as expected, plus (d) because of its category-only control row. On the real tree, all 28 new tests pass. |
| R5-2 mutations | PASS | Breaking the artist display fails test (f) and its unit test. Making any string count as a value fails 10 tests. Dropping only `trim` fails 4, including (d). `[""]` still passes under that one, as A said, because `""` is empty even without `trim`. |
| R5-3 gate | PASS | From a clean state the full verify command exits 0. Renderer 107/107, main 42/42, E2E 7/7, and E2E with `--retries=0` is also 7/7. Biome has 0 errors. I checked the two `FileList.tsx` warnings myself: they existed before and only moved down 9 lines. |
| R5-4 contract-only file is Tagged | PASS | The file tagged by ffmpeg with only a comment shows `Tagged`, and the one with only Category `DOORWood` set in the editor does too. ffprobe, music-metadata and the raw chunk dump agree. On the old `7879ee0` build the same folder shows no badges, so the check tells old from new. Clicking a row opens the editor. |
| R5-5 emptied value stays untagged | PASS | `blank.wav` shows `Tagged` after Category `x` is saved, and loses it after Category is cleared, saved and rescanned. The empty category tag stays in the file, as decision D-10 expects. |
| R5-6 regressions | PASS | A title-only file shows `Tagged`. A file with artists A and B shows `A` in the Artist column. Sorting by Artist still renders all rows. |
| R5-7 file ownership | PASS | Only the four allowed files changed. The `FileList.tsx` diff is just the import, the badge line and the removed function. No `any`, ignore directives or comments were added. |

**Bugs found (both low, for B to schedule):**
- **C-R5-01 – false `Tagged` badge:** a WAV whose INFO values are only NUL bytes shows `Tagged`, although ffprobe sees them as empty. Recorders often write empty fields this way. The badge rule's `trim()` doesn't remove NUL characters. B decides whether to fix this in the reader or in `hasAnyTagValue`.
- **C-R5-02 – NUL kept on read (older bug, in `metadata.ts`, which was frozen this round):** reading metadata keeps the terminating NUL byte. In the main R5-4 test, the Comment field shows `"მძიმე კარი\u0000"` while ffprobe shows the clean text. This is the cause of C-R5-01. I did not check whether a later save writes the NUL back into the file.

I did not record a hash of the source when I started, so I can't prove by hash that it didn't change during my work. What I can say: `git status` showed the same four files at the start and at the end. The diff and new file I read at the start match the end state. I recorded the end hashes for root to compare.

Files are in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/tag-manager-loop/`:
- c-round-5.md
- c-round-5.json
- c-round-5/
